A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ClaraVid dataset and Delentropic Scene Profile (DSP) study. Their complete main texts and supplementary materials are readable, and corresponding equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original ClaraVid reconstruction benchmarks, viewpoint-generalization experiments, synthetic-to-real segmentation results, and scene-complexity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Dronescapes segmentation, UAVid reconstruction experiments, entropy-comparator evaluations, and failure cases.

M1.justification: DSP still computes gradient-based delentropy and models its scene-level distribution with a four-parameter Beta distribution fitted by maximum likelihood. Reconstruction models and semantic heads are retained. Newly specified filtering and histogram settings document implementation details without establishing a procedural revision.

E1.justification: v2 adds Dronescapes to semantic-segmentation evaluation and extends UAVid coverage to reconstruction on six continuous-video sequences with non-grid trajectories. UAVid previously appeared in segmentation and distribution-model motivation. ClaraVid and the existing Mill19/UrbanScene3D analyses remain.

E2.justification: Shannon pixel entropy and GLCM texture entropy become directly evaluated competitors to delentropy in Figure 4, with corresponding comparisons on UAVid in Figure 6. v1 discussed these alternatives without this quantitative comparison. The original reconstruction baselines and ClaraVid-versus-Syndrone segmentation comparison are retained.

E3.justification: Supplementary Section 10.4 introduces a UAVid reconstruction protocol using six 901-frame sequences, specified training/testing frame offsets, stationary-frame exclusion, endpoint inclusion, twofold downsampling, and COLMAP. Section 4 also revises reported point-cloud sampling units from meters to centimeters. These changes do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparative validation of the complexity proxy, robustness evaluation under UAVid's unstructured capture conditions, and two illustrated failure cases involving blur/registration and incomplete coverage. Supplementary Section 8.2 additionally reports resolution- and scene-area-sensitivity observations. The original viewpoint ablation is retained.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 and Figure 4 newly describe and compare predictive-interval widths for the entropy measures. This is a limited reporting addition: interval construction and coverage are unspecified, and neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds entropy-comparator correlations, six-sequence UAVid reconstruction results in Table 5, and Dronescapes segmentation results in Table 4, including mIoU 37.30 for ClaraVid training versus 34.11 for Syndrone training. Matched numerical entries in Tables 2–3 and the existing Table 4 rows are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the gradient, deldensity, delentropy, Beta-profile, and maximum-likelihood definitions. The expanded complexity-profile framing and acquisition-condition discussion provide conceptual explanation and applicability qualifications, without substantively changing the mathematics or adding proofs.

C1.justification: The central ClaraVid and DSP-correlation claims remain. v2 emphasizes complexity estimation from 2D measurements before reconstruction, recasts the third introductory contribution as demonstrating both dataset and DSP utility, and removes the introduction/conclusion's explicit method-selection and pipeline-optimization promise.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's general uncertainty discussion, v2 explicitly qualifies DSP's reliability under blur, resolution changes, unbounded scenes, spatial contraction, and mismatched acquisition policies. The UAVid analysis explains weaker correlations through capture artifacts and incomplete coverage, while Supplementary Section 8.2 specifies conditions for meaningful cross-scene comparison.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Gaussian preprocessing with a 3×3 kernel and sigma 1.0, 3×3 Sobel filters, and 256 histogram bins per axis. It also clarifies depth rendering, reduced segmentation palettes, Zip-NeRF reimplementation, and UAVid setup, and states that code/data are available rather than promising release after acceptance. Conversely, v1's method-of-moments/Newton–Raphson fitting details disappear.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Dronescapes, InfoNeRF, aerial tracking/LiDAR work, evaluation metrics, and COLMAP, while removing the OMMO reference. It explicitly distinguishes image-only DSP estimation from complexity computed during or after reconstruction. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v2 substantially revises the introductory/DSP framing and experimental discussion, reorganizes the dataset description into labeled paragraphs, moves the Beta-distribution motivation from the main text to Supplementary Section 8.1, and consolidates segmentation settings within the experimental-setup appendix. These changes reshape the explanation and organization beyond simply inserting results.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redesigned with normalized entropy axes and overlaid comparators; new UAVid correlation and failure-case figures and Table 5 are added. Table 2 gains complexity-based ordering and color shading. The final RGB montage is replaced by an eight-mission multimodal overview, while several retained figures and tables are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central DSP contribution by addressing v1's lack of direct entropy-baseline comparisons and adding original real-video reconstruction validation, explicit failure conditions, and reproducible computation details. These gains improve evidential support and appropriate use of the metric. Localized reporting problems remain: the new Dronescapes entropy results contradict the retained all-dataset superiority claim, and the domain-gap averages still reflect the earlier three-dataset evaluation. These inconsistencies temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial validation and documentation gains.
